reason: The fibroblast conditions explicitly direct stem-cell descendants toward cells that make connective tissue.
expectation: A subset of the stem-cell descendants will become fibroblasts through the staged differentiation process.

alternatives.reason: The separate muscle lineage also addresses an initial goal.

effect: The fibroblast lineage now has collagen RNA messages, suggesting amino acids can supply the building blocks for collagen production.
reaction: The link from activated genes to RNA at the rough ER is clear.
reason: Collagen is a protein, so the lineage cells need amino acids to make it.
expectation: The cells will use the amino acids and collagen messages to produce collagen protein.

alternatives.reason: I could develop the separate muscle lineage first.

effect: The fibroblasts have made collagen precursors and packaged them in secretory vesicles; the remaining step is likely secretion and extracellular processing.
reaction: The progression from RNA to packaged protein is clear.
reason: Extracellular fluid contains the processing enzymes and space where the supporting material can form.
expectation: The fibroblasts will secrete collagen precursors for processing into extracellular supporting material.

alternatives.reason: I could start the separate muscle lineage first.

effect: The fibroblasts secreted and assembled collagen-rich matrix, completing the supporting-material goal; the muscle lineage remains.
reaction: The distinction between living cells and their surrounding matrix is useful.
reason: The skeletal-muscle conditions explicitly direct a separate subset of stem-cell descendants toward muscle precursors.
expectation: The selected descendants will progress through the staged muscle lineage to muscle precursors.

effect: The muscle branch has committed cells with muscle-protein messages, but no mature fibres yet.
reaction: The shared DNA and different active genes make the contrast between the two lineages clear.
reason: As with collagen production, amino acids should supply the building blocks for the proteins specified by these messages.
expectation: The cells will make muscle proteins and progress toward muscle precursors.

effect: The muscle-lineage cells made muscle proteins and became separate, single-nucleus myoblasts, completing the goal without becoming mature fibres.
reaction: The contrast between retained muscle proteins and exported collagen was useful, though the two overlapping picture descriptions felt repetitive.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the collagen-rich extracellular matrix was most worthwhile: the planned sequence connected protein secretion and processing to the material surrounding living cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final muscle-precursor result repeated much of its picture description in a second wonder, adding little to the distinction between myoblasts and mature fibres.

surprise.text: The same amino-acid supply produced different proteins in the two lineages because they used different RNA messages; the muscle products remained in cells while collagen was exported.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary. The muscle-lineage combination followed the same protein-building logic established for collagen.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the contrast between the two lineages was clear, and the unfinished development of the myoblasts leaves a question about how mature muscle forms.
